set.body:
Scheduling lane: release. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

2026-09-19 operative acceptance amendment (docs/refactor/PLAN.md):
HTML/migration remains useful after the table/API preview. Do not delete historical serializers or run-arm.sh until each historical arm has a replay/parity replacement; no preview dependency on viewer or benchmark campaign.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
HTML/migration remains useful after the table/API preview. Do not delete historical serializers or run-arm.sh until each historical arm has a replay/parity replacement; no preview dependency on viewer or benchmark campaign.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-18-best-recall-to-video-mapper.md §3 Phase 2 recall-map.

The report makes a mapping inspectable; the benchmark's mapper arms move onto the command.

Scope:
Report, migration, retirement.

Acceptance criteria:
1. recall-map writes a self-contained HTML report showing, per unit, the mapping, alternatives and reliability status; every posterior row and flow marginal it displays shows the displayed mass plus the retained remainder (E0's display court).
2. Every mapper arm in the Phase 1b leaderboards regenerates through recall-map (non-mapper rows such as Heusser, LLM labellers and human ceilings are out of scope).
3. run-arm.sh and its environment variables are removed; the tools README points to recall-map.

Gate (AGENTS.md SD2/SD6): `sbt -batch clean compileAll testAll` on the merge result, then
`sbt -batch scalafmtCheckAll scalafmtSbtCheck` as a separate run; every test task in build.sbt's
testAll alias reports bound totals (56 at 0e36a7fa, after the corpus modules were added; recount if
modules change); a named mutation witness per new guard, and each compile-time-probe mutation proved
after its own clean recompile; `cd docs-site && npm run verify:examples` when public API or examples
change; fresh-context cold review in a separate pass; the commit body states the evidence and what
it does not establish.

Size: M.

2026-09-22 operative workflow reconciliation (docs/plans/2026-09-22-recall-encoding-workflow.md):
Repository ownership is corrected: StoryAtlas owns the self-contained HTML recall report through its existing portable-bundle ticket bd-01M19JQRMYBTYJN7V9HPN7DYKQ and static-publication mechanics bd-01M1C2TTHJRV7BWMQMPS7ENR1D. M1 selected-view save/export remains bounded and does not acquire a full portable HTML-report requirement. This StoryModel ticket owns canonical CLI artifacts, the explicit consumer handoff, benchmark-arm migration and retirement of legacy launchers. Replace original criterion 1's StoryModel HTML writer with a checked report artifact/handoff consumed by StoryAtlas; retain displayed mass plus retained remainder in the producer contract and exact-pair consumer evidence before claiming report integration. Keep all historical arm replay/parity requirements: no serializer or run-arm.sh is removed until every in-scope historical mapper arm has an evidenced replacement. Research/benchmark prerequisites here do not block M1 or basic temporal inspection. Full film-model V1 remains separate.
set.title: [release] CLI/benchmark migration and StoryAtlas report handoff; retire legacy arms only after parity
